reconstructed_theorem_text:
Let H,K be real complete Hilbert spaces and assume H is explicitly separable. Let D:H->partialLinear[R] K be a genuine real-linear partial operator on its actual submodule domain, with D.IsClosed (actual closed graph). Fix f:H. Let epsilon:N->R have epsilon_n>0 for every n and tend atTop to0 in R; monotonicity is not assumed. Let u:N->D.domain be a supplied actual solution family.
Assume for EVERY n and EVERY v:D.domain,
  epsilon_n*<u_n,v>_H+<D(u_n),D(v)>_K=<f,v>_H.
Assume for EVERY v:D.domain, D(v)=0 implies <f,v>_H=0. This is forcing orthogonality to every element of the actual kernel of this SAME partial operator.
Then BOTH limits hold simultaneously in genuine norm topologies:
  epsilon_n scalar-multiplied by (u_n as H) tends atTop to0 in H,
  epsilon_n scalar-multiplied by D(u_n) tends atTop to0 in K.
D is fixed before f,epsilon and solutions; this theorem applies to every supplied family satisfying all the actual variational equations. It does not construct another family. H and K need not be finite-dimensional; K separability, dense domain, bounded operator, supplied cluster/graph/limit certificate, or uniform unscaled-solution bound is not assumed. Ordinary product maxnorm is not silently identified with a Hilbert product. There is no abstract mean-zero replacement for all-kernel orthogonality and no assumption that solutions are centered. Both scalings are epsilon_n, not sqrt(epsilon_n). No rate, unscaled convergence, epsilon=0 solution, range/spectral-gap/further inequality or jointly measurable selection is concluded.
objects: Real complete Hilbert H,K;explicit separable H;SAME actual closed partial linear D;forcing f;positive-to-zero epsilon;supplied domain solution family;scaled function/gradient sequences.
domains: H,K complete real Hilbert not necessarily finite-dimensional,H separable explicitly,K separability not required. D actual real partial operator on submodule domain with closed graph. u:N->D.domain,epsilon:N->R. Inner products H/K and atTop neighborhoods0 in genuine norm topologies. No maxnorm-product/Hilbert-product conflation.
quantifiers: Universal H,K,separable H,D closed,f,positive-to-zero epsilon,supplied u. Variational forall n and all domain v;orthogonality forall kernel v in domain. BOTH limits same family.D fixed before f/epsilon/u,no constructed alternative family.
assumptions: Actual complete Hilbert structures and H separability;D.IsClosed;epsilon_n>0 every n,Tendsto epsilon0;all-domain variational equations;f orthogonal to EVERY v with Dv=0. No monotonicity,density,boundedness,mean-zero shortcut,cluster/limit certificate or uniform unscaled bound.
conclusion: epsilon_n*u_n tends strongly0 in H AND epsilon_n*D(u_n) tends strongly0 in K for same supplied solution family.
scopes: Both true strong norm limits,exact epsilon scaling,not weak/pointwise/unscaled. Orthogonality actual entire kernel,not presumed centered u. No solution construction,epsilon0/range/spectral-gap/further inequality or measurable selection.
constant_dependencies: epsilon_n any positive nonmonotone decay0;both scale factors epsilon_n,not square root. Unit gradient/RHS variational coefficients.No estimate constant/rate.H and K typed zeros distinct,D/f fixed.
